title: smart-routing-fallback-regional-failover-debug-notes
content:
Incident breadcrumbs -- smart routing / fallback / regional failover

Context:
- Date: 2025-10-12 (initial) -> followups through 2025-10-15
- Symptoms: sudden spike in 5xxs for requests routed to eu-west-1 for model: rw-large-v2; automated fallback to rw-large-v1 triggered but many requests still failing with 502/504. Customers reporting intermittent timeouts.
- Affected surface: hosted-api (edge routing), Dedicated customers in eu-west-1 (some requests), internal canary traffic.
- Short hypothesis: either region capacity depletion + routing controller incorrectly marking variants as incompatible, or healthchecks flapping in the regional node pool causing Envoy to route to unhealthy backends.

What I ran (commands & quick outputs)
1) quick check of edge errors:
- curl to metrics endpoint: curl -sS "https://api.redwood.dev/metrics?service=edge" | jq '.errors_by_region["eu-west-1"]' -> 503 count spike ~ 14:30-14:45 UTC

2) repro with trace header (to follow request path):
- curl -v -H "X-Request-Id: oc-req-20251012-01" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate?model=rw-large-v2
  -> Response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
  -> Response body (snippet): "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers
  connection failure"

3) check routing-controller logs (k8s):
- kubectl -n routing logs deploy/routing-controller --since=3h | grep "oc-req-20251012" -A5 -B3
  -> found route decision: fallback invoked, target set to rw-large-v1@eu-west-1a. 
  -> several WARN entries: "instance selection: insufficient healthy instances in eu-west-1 (available=0, required=1)"

4) inspect cluster nodes & pods in eu-west-1 node pool:
- kubectl get nodes --selector=region=eu-west-1 -o wide
  -> nodes: 6 ready, but two showing "NotReady" briefly around 14:35 (see node-status-snippet below)
- kubectl get pods -n serving --field-selector spec.nodeName=ip-10-0-45-12 | wc -l -> 0 (drained?)

5) node status snippet (from kube-controller logs):
- Node ip-10-0-45-12 status changed: Ready -> NotReady (Kubelet stopped) at 14:34:11 UTC
- Reason: kubelet OOMKilled? (need full kubelet logs)

6) envoy logs for a failing backend (pod id: backend-77f6b8d6):
- kubectl -n serving logs backend-77f6b8d6 -c envoy | tail -n 40
  -> several entries: "upstream response timeout" and "upstream connection failure: TLS handshake"

7) model process health inside pod (rw-large-v2):
- kubectl -n serving exec -it backend-77f6b8d6 -- ps aux | grep model_server -> model_server present
- but logs show repeated "OOM: failed to allocate KV cache" around the same window -> possible memory pressure from incoming burst or bad batching config.

8) control plane checks (routing decision engine):
- GET /admin/routing/status?region=eu-west-1 -> returns {"healthy_instances":0, "fallback_policy":"model_variant_fallback,regional_failover"} (admin API returned JSON; see admin log snippet)
- toggled fallback: POST /admin/routing/override {"region":"eu-west-1","force_route":"rw-large-v1"} -> immediate drop in 502s for rw-large-v1 targets, but rw-large-v2 still failing when targeted.

9) quick verification of LB / DNS
- dig edge.eu-west-1.redwood.dev -> correct A records
- curl directly to node ip (bypassing LB) still produced 504 on rw-large-v2: suggests issue is upstream (pod/model) not edge DNS.

Error snippets (collected)
- "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers"
- "upstream response timeout"
- "error: KV cache allocation failed: cannot allocate 2.3GB"
- kubelet logs: "OOMKilled: process: runc-shim" (need to correlate container oom kills)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Memory pressure on model pods (rw-large-v2) in eu-west-1 caused kubelet/container OOMs -> Envoy sees backend down -> routing controller treats region as degraded -> fallback kicks in. Evidence: OOM-like logs, model server KV allocation failures, NotReady node events.
2) Autoscaler / HPA misconfigured for rw-large-v2 in eu-west-1 causing insufficient replica counts during burst -> available_instances=0. Evidence: HPA metrics show CPU requests saturated; replicas remained at 2 while desired was 6 per metrics at spike time.
3) Faulty healthcheck config or flapping healthchecks: healthcheck endpoints returning 200 sometimes but timed out under load -> Envoy marks as unhealthy. Evidence: envoy upstream timeout logs + intermittent 200s.
4) Control plane bug: routing-controller incorrectly aggregates health across AZs causing false "available=0" when only one AZ degraded. Evidence: routing logs show "available=0" but there were healthy pods in other AZs -- need to confirm labels/affinity.

Quick root-cause triage steps done:
- Pulled kubelet logs for NotReady node -> found repeated container OOMKilled events at 14:33-14:36.
- Scaled rw-large-v2 Deployment in eu-west-1 from 2->4 replicas manually (kubectl scale deployment/rw-large-v2 --replicas=4) -> partial reduction in 502s for a short window, but OOMs continued on some nodes.
- Temporarily adjusted batch_size in runtime config to reduce peak memory (applied via configmap and rollout) -> immediate reduction in KV allocation failures in logs.
- Updated HPA target CPU from 70%->60% to encourage earlier scaling (HPA settings under review).

Open questions / next actions:
- Get full kubelet logs and container runtime logs for ip-10-0-45-12 and ip-10-0-45-13 for 14:20-14:50 window. (Action: SRE - Ravi)
- Correlate OOMKilled events to specific container images/versions (are we running a bad rw-large-v2 build that regresses memory?). (Action: Olivia + Applied ML)
- Review HPA and node pool sizing for eu-west-1; consider increasing buffer and burst capacity. (Action: infra)
- Investigate routing-controller aggregation logic: why did it report 0 available while AZ-level healthy pods existed? (Action: Olivia)
- Add guardrail to admin API to avoid full-region failover when only single-AZ degraded -- prefer cross-AZ balancing. (Action: routing team)
- Postmortem draft: collect timeline, metrics, impacted customers, mitigation steps. (Action: Olivia)

Notes to self (quick):
- When testing, include X-Request-Id and reduce sampling to capture full traces from edge -> routing-controller -> envoy -> model pod.
- Reproduce locally with small model to validate heap usage per request under similar batching config.
- Check commit history around 2025-10-01 for any changes to memory allocations in runtime (PRs: /pull/457, /pull/468).

Timeline (short):
- 14:30 UTC: first 5xx alerts from EU hosted endpoints (rw-large-v2).
- 14:33-14:36 UTC: node NotReady events + kubelet OOMKilled.
- 14:37 UTC: auto-fallback engaged to rw-large-v1 per routing-controller.
- 14:45 UTC: manual scale and batch_size change partially mitigates.
- 15:10 UTC: still intermittent failures; decided to keep reduced batch_size until HPA/infra changes deployed.

Quick links/reference snippets (for postmortem):
- routing-controller log excerpt saved to /tmp/routing-logs-20251012.txt
- kubelet logs saved to /tmp/kubelet-eu-west-1-14-33-14-36.txt
- envoy logs for backend-77f6b8d6 saved to /tmp/envoy-backend-77f6b8d6.txt

If anything else I should collect now:
- full dmesg from affected nodes; check for kernel OOM killer.
- container cgroup memory metrics around time window.
- detailed HPA metrics and metrics-server scraped values.

End of scratchpad.

(Will convert into formal incident writeup once SRE and Applied ML confirm root cause.)
